sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Westland, Michigan?
sections.html:
The City of Westland bills and collects its own property tax through the Finance Department at City Hall, 36300 Warren Road, Westland, MI 48185. The Finance Director serves as the city's Treasurer by charter. Wayne County is the county the city sits in, and the county treasurer takes over unpaid bills after the city's collection period ends.

For bill questions the tax billing line is 734-467-3172, and the Finance Department is at 734-467-3169. Both are open Monday through Friday from 9 am to 5 pm. The Assessor's Office, at the same address on 734-467-3160, sets the values that the bills are based on, and it says inquiries are answered by the end of the next business day.

Deeds are not recorded at City Hall. They go to the Wayne County Register of Deeds in downtown Detroit, which is a separate office from either city department.

sections.h2: When are Westland property taxes due?
sections.html:
Westland mails bills twice a year, on July 1 and December 1, and they are due on August 15 and February 14. When a due date falls on a weekend, the next business day applies, unless City Council extends the deadline.

Council has used the extension power more than once. For summer 2026 it pushed the no-penalty deadline to Monday, August 31, 2026, and that date has passed. The city's notice told owners who did not receive a bill to call 734-467-3172. Because extensions are decided by vote each year, read the notice on the city's website rather than relying on the printed due date.

Owners who need more time on the summer bill can ask for a deferral. The city has an online application that goes to the Tax Clerk by email, by mail to City Hall, or by drop box.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Westland tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay online through the city's Taxes payment portal, by phone, or in person. The method decides whether you pay a fee.

  • By phone, call the Point and Pay automated service at 844-400-3556. It charges a 3% service fee.
  • In person, pay at City Hall during business hours.
  • Two drop boxes at City Hall take non-cash payments only: checks, money orders and cashier's checks. Put everything in a sealed envelope.
  • The white drop box is on the northeast side of the parking lot, next to the postal mailbox, and needs no postage. A wall slot sits just east of the main entrance.

A seller closing close to a due date should ask the title company to pay from the proceeds and to get a receipt. Most bills in a closing are prorated between buyer and seller, but the title company still needs the current amount from the city.

sections.h2: How does Westland assess a house?
sections.html:
The Assessor values every parcel each year, and state law sets the assessment at 50% of true cash value as of December 31. The tax bill itself is figured from taxable value, not assessed value, times the local millage rates, so a voter-approved millage increase changes the bill even when the assessment stands still.

The city explains three methods. The sales comparison approach studies recent sales of comparable homes. The cost approach prices what it would take to replace the property with current labor and materials, less depreciation. The income approach is used for rentals. For 2026 assessments the sales window runs from April 2023 through March 2025, and it leaves out bank sales and foreclosures since those are not arm's-length transactions.

One rule surprises sellers: neither the Assessor nor the Board of Review may raise or lower an assessment based only on the sale price. A buyer's price is evidence, but not the whole case. The city also posts its economic condition factor and land value analyses online, and owners can look up taxable value, taxes owed, a map and the legal description for any parcel on the city's assessment site.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Westland assessment?
sections.html:
Appeal to the March Board of Review, which the city calls the only time a taxpayer can appeal a residential home value. Assessment notices go out near the end of February, about fourteen days before the board's first meeting, and they list the hearing dates and hours.

  • Complete a Petition to the Board of Review for each parcel. Incomplete petitions come back.
  • Book an appointment, which cannot happen until notices are mailed. Slots run in five minute intervals. You may instead appeal by letter.
  • Attach proof of value: an appraisal, sales comparables, a market analysis or photos. Both methods carry equal weight, and no decision is made during the appointment itself.
  • Get everything in before 1:00 pm on the last day of the scheduled meetings.
  • An attorney, accountant or agent may appear for you with a written authorization signed by you and the representative.

The board has three members and two alternates, appointed by the Mayor and confirmed by Council. It meets in organizational session on the Tuesday after the first Monday in March, in the Council Chambers. It can review the current year's assessed value, poverty exemptions under MCL 211.7u and the assessment classification, and it also corrects clerical errors and mutual mistakes of fact.

sections.h2: What happens when Westland tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
After the city's collection period, unpaid real property tax moves to the Wayne County Treasurer. The county says taxes not paid to the local treasurer by the last day of February become delinquent on the following March 1, and after that they can be paid only at the county office, 400 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, in Detroit.

The county describes the path in plain terms. A parcel delinquent for one year reaches forfeited status the next March 1. Interest rises from 1% to 1.5% per month, retroactive, and a $175 foreclosure fee and $30 in recording fees are added. The county sends at least ten written notices before foreclosure, and it offers payment plans for owners who cannot pay in full. A foreclosed parcel is offered to local governments for the minimum bid, then goes to public auction in September and October.

A seller with a delinquent balance can usually clear it from sale proceeds. Ask the Wayne County Treasurer for a payoff figure rather than estimating, because interest runs monthly.

sections.h2: What does a Westland seller file after the sale?
sections.html:
The buyer must notify the assessing office of the transfer within 45 days on the state's form, per MCL 211.27a. It states the parties, the date, the actual consideration and the parcel number. Title companies commonly supply the form at closing.

The reason it matters to sellers is the cap. Taxable value on a home can rise only by a limited yearly figure while one owner holds it, then resets toward assessed value the year after a transfer. A buyer's first bill can therefore be well above the seller's last one. If you claimed the principal residence exemption, file the state's rescind form for the property you sold. Ask the Westland Assessor's Office for the current forms and for the status of your exemption.

sections.h2: What should a Westland seller know about the city itself?
sections.html:
Westland is a western suburb of Detroit, about 18 miles from downtown, and it covers 20.43 square miles of land. It was part of Nankin Township, which grew quickly after World War II. The Norwayne subdivision, built right after the war to house returning soldiers who worked in nearby factories, is one of the oldest areas. Westland Shopping Center opened in 1965, and township voters created the City of Westland on May 16, 1966.

Schools come from several districts. Most of the city is in the Wayne-Westland Community School District, the northern edge is in Livonia Public Schools, and small southern pieces fall in the Taylor and Romulus districts.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 82,333 residents, down from 85,420 in the 2020 census. In 2020 to 2024 data, 61.3% of housing is owner-occupied, the median value of an owner-occupied home is $184,600, median gross rent is $1,158, and the city has 35,932 households averaging 2.30 people. Median household income is $62,076.

faqs.q: What are the Westland property tax due dates?
faqs.a: Summer bills go out July 1 and are due August 15. Winter bills go out December 1 and are due February 14. City Council can extend either date, as it did for summer 2026 when it set August 31, 2026.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Westland tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the tax billing office at 734-467-3172, open Monday through Friday from 9 am to 5 pm at City Hall, 36300 Warren Road. The Finance Department line is 734-467-3169.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Westland assessment?
faqs.a: In March, before the March Board of Review. Notices come near the end of February with hearing dates. File a petition for each parcel, book an appointment or send a letter, and attach evidence of value.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to pay my Westland taxes by phone?
faqs.a: Yes. The Point and Pay phone service at 844-400-3556 charges a 3% service fee. Paying at City Hall or in a drop box with a check or money order has no listed fee.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Westland taxes after they turn delinquent?
faqs.a: At the Wayne County Treasurer, 400 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Detroit. Tax unpaid by the end of February becomes delinquent on March 1 and can be paid only to the county from then on.
